paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.
model_annotation: The horizontal grouped bar chart illustrates the distribution of conversations classified by whether participants were deceived (“Yes,” “Partially,” or “No”) across four scenarios. The category axis is the vertical (y) axis, listing scenarios from top to bottom as Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism, with no stated sorting rule beyond this displayed order. The value axis is the horizontal (x) axis labeled “Number of Conversations,” shown on a linear scale with tick labels at regular intervals of 10 (0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60), and bars extending slightly beyond 60 for the largest value. Each scenario contains three adjacent (non-stacked) horizontal bars distinguished by color per the legend titled “Deceived”: red for “Yes,” yellow for “Partially,” and green for “No.” In Academic Collaboration, the red “Yes” bar is approximately 35 conversations, the yellow “Partially” bar about 27, and the green “No” bar about 7. In Recruitment, the red “Yes” bar is about 37, the yellow “Partially” bar about 24, and the green “No” bar about 6. In Academic Funding, the red “Yes” bar extends to roughly 66, while the yellow “Partially” and green “No” bars are short at about 4 and about 3, respectively. In Journalism, the red “Yes” bar is about 15, the yellow “Partially” bar about 48, and the green “No” bar about 6. No individual bars appear to be specially emphasized with annotations or outlines beyond the standard color coding and the legend.
